A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SEM-CTRL work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–H. Reformatting and added end matter do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark experiments, component ablations, computational-efficiency measurements and fine-tuning results in Sections 4–5 and Appendix H.

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark experiments, ablations, computational-efficiency measurements and fine-tuning results in Sections 4–5 and Appendix H.

M1.justification: The ASG constraint mechanism, vocabulary alignment, token-level MCTS, reward function and caching strategies in Section 3 are unchanged. No algorithmic component or generation procedure is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic grammar tasks, graph coloring, Sudoku 3×3 and 4×4, Blocksworld planning and JSON parsing. The new discussion of multimodal applications introduces no evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same Base, BoN and MCTS constraint variants, o1-preview, DeepSeek-R1 and o4-mini comparisons, and JSON-specific XGrammar baseline. Appendix E retains the same comparator list.

E3.justification: The stated protocols remain unchanged, including 30 samples per synthetic grammar task, 600 Blocksworld problems, the 50-problem ablation set, model sizes, evaluation metrics, sampling budgets and fine-tuning data fractions.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same component ablations in Tables 3, 14 and 15, fine-tuning analysis in Table 6 and soft-accuracy analysis in Appendix H.3. The added limitations discussion includes no new robustness tests or case studies.

E5.justification: Both report averaging over three runs with the same Blocksworld exception, paired permutation tests at alpha = 0.05, and standard deviations in Table 13. No statistical procedure or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All corresponding main-text and appendix result tables retain their entries and numerical values. For example, Table 1 retains SEM-CTRL Blocksworld accuracies of 74.0% for Llama 1B and 96.8% for Llama 70B. Reported rankings and experimental findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Definitions 3.1–3.3, Equations (1)–(9), the semantic-validity argument, vocabulary-mapping consistency condition and Appendix B's ASP account are retained. The added applicability discussion introduces no revised formal assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims about combining ASGs with token-level MCTS, guaranteeing semantic validity and enabling small models to compete with larger reasoning models without fine-tuning.

C2.justification: v4 adds a Broader Impact Statement covering possible degradation with unfamiliar constraint vocabulary, text-only evaluation, unvalidated multimodal extension and limitations of binary validity. It also discusses constraint-induced bias, distinguishes formal correctness from ethical suitability, and proposes symbolic transparency as an auditing mechanism.

D1.justification: The prompts, ASG examples, sampling parameters and hardware specifications in Appendices A, D, F and G remain unchanged. The code-release footnote still promises future release; no new implementation or code-access instructions are supplied.

R1.justification: The same 57 referenced works and Section 6 research positioning are retained. Alphabetical reference ordering and changed Zhang 2023a/2023b labels reflect bibliographic formatting. The Broader Impact Statement reuses previously cited work on generating ASP specifications.

P1.justification: v4 adds Broader Impact Statement and Acknowledgments sections after the conclusion, updates publication metadata and changes citation presentation and reference ordering. The existing scientific prose and main-text and appendix section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The TMLR template changes the title and author arrangement, running headers, spacing and float placement. Figures 1–2 are enlarged, and appendix tables shift across pages. The eight figures and fifteen tables retain their substantive content and organization.

improvement.justification: The added Broader Impact Statement makes applicability limits and bias risks more explicit, particularly that formal correctness does not ensure ethical suitability. This modestly improves transparency. The scientific evidence and reproducibility documentation remain unchanged, and the asserted environmental and auditing benefits receive no additional empirical validation.
